subject: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology - prompt sets / eval harness
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology - prompt sets / eval harness

Tom — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Target SLOs you called out
   - 95th pct latency ≤ 400ms for streaming token latency
   - p50 latency ≤ 120ms for short responses (<= 64 tokens)
   - Throughput: sustained 120 reqs/sec at concurrency 40 for our chat use-case
   - Cold-start: reclaimable model instance in < 60s (for Dedicated scaling tests)

2) What we need from EdgeFin to reproduce your workload
   - Representative prompt set (you mentioned ~1.2k prompts across short/medium/long)
   - Expected token distribution and avg response length per prompt category
   - Streaming vs non-streaming traffic split (you estimated 70% streaming)

3) Redwood deliverables
   - Benchmark methodology doc (measurement definitions, warmup, caches, reproducibility checklist) — attached the initial spec (redwood_benchmark_spec_v1.pdf)
   - Example run config + eval harness skeleton (run_config_example.yaml)
   - We'll ingest your prompt set and run a first pass on a Dedicated pool that matches your target instance type, then share raw metrics + aggregated dashboard.

Next steps / ask
   - Can you send the prompt set and token distribution? (edgefin_prompt_set_v2.jsonl is great if you have it)
   - If you want us to run the benchmark next week, please confirm: preferred window (PST mornings preferred for us) and whether SRE should be on the call for live troubleshooting.

I've attached the spec and run config as a starting point. We'll iterate on measurement definitions once we have your prompts.

Thanks — looking forward.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

- I've attached our prompt export (edgefin_prompt_set_v2.jsonl) — it's ~1.2k items and includes a short/medium/long tag on each line. The file also has the expected avg response length field per prompt.
- Streaming split is closer to 65% in production, but 70% is fine for the first run.
- Preferred window: Tue/Wed next week, 9am-12pm PST. SRE will join the call for the initial run.

A few clarifying Qs from our side before you run anything: 
1) When you say "streaming token latency" — is that time-to-first-token or inter-token latency? For us the critical one is time-to-first-token but we also care about steady-state inter-token latency for streaming UX smoothness.
2) For throughput tests do you simulate realistic think-time between messages or do you replay constant QPS?

We can join a short 30-min sync Monday to align on these measurement definitions if that helps.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology - prompt sets / eval harness

Tom / Marissa — digging into this now. Quick answers to the two questions and how we measure: 

1) Streaming metrics
   - We report both time-to-first-token (TTFT) and inter-token latency (mean & 95th). For clarity in the benchmark report we'll surface: TTFT_p50, TTFT_p95, inter_token_p50, inter_token_p95.
   - "Streaming token latency <= 400ms (95th)" in the recap maps to TTFT_p95 <= 400ms. We'll add inter-token p95 target to the spec (suggested threshold: 80ms).

2) Throughput load profile
   - We support both constant QPS replay and realistic think-time scenarios. For qualification we recommend two passes: a replayed constant-QPS run to validate max sustainable throughput, and a trace-replay run (with your think-time distribution) to validate end-to-end SLOs under realistic load.

Methodology notes we will apply (and include in the final spec):
   - Warmup: 5 minutes of traffic to populate caches (or 2x typical prefix appearance for KV caches), then reset counters and run measurement windows.
   - Concurrency: use client-side workers to reach target concurrency levels; ensure each worker uses a fresh connection to exercise networking and runtime paths.
   - Reproducibility: we include seed files, run configs, exact model version, quantization profile, and kernel selection in the run artifact.

We'll stage a draft benchmark run today on an internal Dedicated pool to sanity-check the prompts and will share raw traces + aggregated dashboard before your SRE call next week.

Proposed Monday 30-min sync: 2026-12-07 10:00 PST — I can grab the calendar invite if that works.

--
